          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
            Being aggrieved by  order dated  26.10.2026 passed by 
the Bombay High Court in Writ Petition (L) No. 35535/2026,  
the petitioner has preferred this Special Leave Petition  
seeking  permission  for  medical  termination  of  her  
pregnancy under Section 3(2)(b) of the Medical Termination  
of Pregnancy Act, 1971 (hereinafter referred to as the `MTP 
Act’).
The impugned order is dated 26.10.2026 by which the  
petitioner’s prayer for seeking termination of pregnancy  
(presently  25  weeks)  made  under  Article  226  of  the  
Constitution of India was rejected. This Special leave  
Petition was filed on 27.10.2026.
We heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned 
counsel for respondent No.2-husband/Caveator and learned  
counsel for respondent No.1/State, who appeared on advance 
notice (on 29.10.2026).
Thereafter, the matter was listed on 02.11.2026 and we 
heard learned counsel for the respective parties extensively 
in the presence of the petitioner and respondent No.2, who 
appeared through Video Conferencing facility and the matter 
was directed to be listed today (04.11.2024) at 02.00 P.M. 
We have heard learned counsel for the respective parties 
in the presence of the petitioner, who has appeared through 
2

## Page 347

Video Conferencing facility and respondent No.2, who has  
appeared in person. 
Having  taken note of the submissions advanced at the Bar
on behalf of the respective parties, we find that having  
regard to the facts and circumstances of this case, the  
prayer sought for by the petitioner herein cannot be granted.
The Special Leave Petition is hence dismissed.
All pleadings filed during the course of hearing before 
this Court shall not be construed to the prejudice of the 
respective parties in any other proceeding.
Pending application(s) shall stand disposed of.
(NEETU SACHDEVA)                                (DIVYA BABBAR)

petitioner would be to firstly approach the jurisdictional High
Court, i.e. the Allahabad High Court.

Court, we direct the Registry of this Court to transfer the
complete original record of this Writ Petition to the Registrar
General  of  the  Allahabad  High  Court.  The  record  shall  be
transferred within two days from the date of this order.

to put up the matter before Hon’ble the Chief Justice of the
Allahabad High Court, even during the course of vacations, if any,
and obtain appropriate orders for listing the case before a
Division Bench of the High Court on 16.11.2026. 
5. The learned Division Bench of the High Court is requested to
pass appropriate orders on the petitioner’s prayer for  interim
relief on the date fixed above.

Writ Petition, apart from filing additional documents before the
High Court, if so advised.

merits,  and  the  petitioner  is  at  liberty  to  raise  all  his

O R D E R
1. Heard Mr. Amit Kumar Pathak, learned counsel appearing for the
review petitioner, and Ms. Aishwarya Bhati, learned Additional
Solicitor General appearing for the State.
2.  The present review petition calls in question the correctness
of the order dated 26.11.2024, whereby this Court allowed the

## Page 430

2
R.P. (C) Nos. 2671-2674/2025
appeal preferred by the State and set aside the order dated
10.05.2023 passed by the learned Single Judge directing the framing
of charges.
3. The review petition has been filed primarily on the ground
that  during  the  proceedings  culminating  in  the  order  dated
26.11.2024, upon a query being posed by this Court, the learned
junior counsel appearing for the review petitioner (who was the
respondent in the main special leave petition) inadvertently stated
that  pay  fixation  had  indeed  been  effected  for  the  review
petitioner on parity with one Shyamal Ganguly and Vimal Kumar
Upreti.
4. The learned counsel for the review petitioner submitted that
the said statement was factually inaccurate and that parity in pay
fixation was not, in fact, extended to the review petitioner with
that of Shyamal Ganguly and Vimal Kumar Upreti. Initially, when the
review petitioner approached the High Court by way of a writ
petition, the learned Single Judge, vide order dated 19.05.2004,
directed as under:
“In the result, the review petition as well as writ
petition,  insofar  as  it  relates  to  the  review
petitioners only are allowed. 
A  writ  in  the  nature  of  mandamus  is  issued
commanding the opposite parties to appoint the review
petitioners on the post of junior clerk, giving them
equal treatment which has been given to similarly
circumstanced persons, namely Shyamal Ganguly and Vimal
Kumar Upreti.”
5. The special appeal preferred against the said order was

## Page 431

3
R.P. (C) Nos. 2671-2674/2025
subsequently disposed of, upon noting that the order passed by the
learned Single Judge stood complied with and had, by efflux of
time, rendered the appeal infructuous. Thereafter, a contempt
petition  was  filed,  which  was  disposed  of  by  recording  the
submission of the learned Standing Counsel for the State, which was
duly concurred with by the learned counsel for the contempt
petitioners as to the effect that orders have been complied with.
6. Subsequently, in the second contempt petition, when charges
were directed to be framed, this Court was approached, which
culminated in the passing of the order dated 26.11.2024.
7. . Having heard the learned counsel for the parties, we are
satisfied that not only before this Court, but even before the High
Court at the stage of the special appeal as also during the first
contempt proceedings, it was not disputed that the orders stood
fully implemented. At this distance of time, we cannot permit the
review petitioner to re-agitate or re-argue the matter on merits.
8. The review petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
9. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.

O R D E R
Heard Mr. G. Arudra Rao, learned counsel for the petitioner
and Mr. Rajan Kumar Chaurasia, learned counsel for the contesting
respondents.
2. Pursuant to a disciplinary inquiry initiated against the
petitioner on 28.05.2025, an order of removal from service was
passed against him. A review petition preferred thereafter was also
rejected by the employer on 25.08.2025.
3. Upon a challenge being mounted in judicial review, the learned
Single Judge dismissed the writ petition on 15.09.2025. Aggrieved
thereby, the petitioner filed an intra-court special appeal. When
the special appeal came up for hearing, the Division Bench of the
High Court, after taking note of the rival contentions, passed the
following order:
“ We, however, feel that even removal from service
is a lighter punishment and we, therefore, give the
appellant  a  notice  to  show  cause  as  to  why  the
punishment  of  removal  from  service  should  not  be
enhanced to that of dismissal from service.”
4. The Division Bench has, by the impugned order, called upon the
appellant to show cause as to why the penalty of removal from
service should not be enhanced to that of dismissal.
5. We are of the opinion that such an order could not have been
passed by the Division Bench. The employer had passed the order of

## Page 437

3
SLP (C) No. 25465/2026
removal, which had attained finality at the instance of the
employer. It is the petitioner alone who was aggrieved thereby, and
having failed before the learned Single Judge, had approached the
Division Bench in appeal.
6. The direction issuing show cause notice for enhancement of
punishment at the instance of the Division Bench is legally
untenable. Consequently, we set aside the impugned order. D.B.
Special Appeal Writ No. 1421/2025 shall now be heard on its own
merits, without reference to the impugned order and uninfluenced by
any observations made therein.
7. The special leave petition stands disposed of in the aforesaid
terms.
8. In respect of the submission of Mr. Arudhra Rao, learned
counsel, that the matter requires expeditious hearing, we observe
that it would be open to the petitioner to make such a prayer
before the High Court.
9. The order impugned in SLP(C) No. 34501/2026 is an order of
adjournment. No separate orders are called for.
10. Pending applications, if any, stand disposed of.

appellant had preferred an appeal before the High Court
of Chhattisgarh at Bilaspur (briefly the ‘High Court’

No.1423 of 2023. By the impugned judgment and order
dated 20.08.2025, the High Court has dismissed the

appellant was taken into custody on 10.01.2020 and has

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.         OF 2026
(arising out of SLP (C) No.  20379/2023)
DISTRICT COLLECTOR & ORS.            ...APPELLANT(S)
                                VERSUS
MULUGORI NARASAMMA (DIED) 
     THR.  LRS. & ORS.                  ...RESPONDENT(S)
O R D E R
1. Leave granted.
2. We have heard the learned counsel for the appellants
and learned Senior Counsel for the respondents.
3. We have also perused the orders passed by the High
Court on two occasions in earlier rounds of litigation,
along with the impugned judgment.
4. It is the case of the appellants that the private
respondents herein, who were impleaded by the High Court
as  the  legal  representatives  (LRs)  of  the  deceased
original writ petitioners, i.e, Mulugori Narasamma and
Mulugori Durgamma, are not their LRs. The High Court
should have verified their claim before impleading them.
They  vehemently  submit  that  the  private  respondents
herein are in no way related to the original writ
petitioners and there is no subsisting cause of action
remaining at all in view of the death of the original
1

## Page 484

writ petitioners. 
4. In view of the above, and upon perusing the judgment
and orders passed by the High Court, we are of the view
that the High Court should have conducted an enquiry to
check the veracity of their claim before impleading them
as LRs. Accordingly, we are inclined to remit the matter
back to the High Court to enquire into and decide
whether the private respondents herein are in fact the
LRs of the original writ petitioners. 
5. In such view of the matter, and to the above
discussed extent alone, the impugned judgment stands set
aside, and the matter is remitted back to the Division
Bench of the High Court for the State of Telangana at
Hyderabad for fresh adjudication.
6. The High Court to pass appropriate orders on the
aforesaid  issue  after  affording  opportunity  to  the
parties concerned within a period of four months from
today.
7. The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
8. Pending applications, if any, shall stand disposed
of.

4. The only issue now is about the place of residence. While
Ms.Ayesha Khan-respondent mother is not willing to live in the
house, where the in-laws and brother-in-law are living. The
other aspect of the matter is the children are studying in
Akola, Maharashtra.
5. We are of the opinion that it should be proper that the
in-laws and the brother-in-law to find an appropriate separate
place, near their residence for Ms.Ayesha Khan and for the
three boys to live so that their education is not disturbed.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner wants time to take
instructions on this aspect.

For Respondent(s)  
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The submission on behalf of the petitioner is that the order
of externment is based on a police report which cites 15 cases; out
of which, 5 were preventive proceedings.  Insofar as the remaining
10 are concerned, in 7 the petitioner has been acquitted/discharged
whereas 3 are under the Excise Act. It is submitted that an offence
punishable under the Excise Act does not find mention in Section 5
of the Chattisgarh State Security Act, 1990.  Besides, in offences
punishable under the Excise Act witnesses are, ordinarily, State
1

## Page 578

officials therefore, any influence on those witnesses is not
possible. Thus, pendency of those cases cannot be a ground for
externment.
2. Issue notice, returnable in six weeks.
3. In the meantime, the effect and operation of the externment
order shall remain stayed.
  (KAVITA PAHUJA)                               (SAPNA BANSAL)

compliance of the direction given in paragraph 8 of our

applied for the post. The candidates who had applied shall
be  categorized  broadly  into  two  categories:  one  who
fulfilled the eligibility criteria strictly as per the
2005 Regulations and the other who fulfilled the broader
eligibility criteria notified in the advertisement.
4. The compliance affidavit shall also indicate whether
any  decision  to  relax  the  eligibility  criteria  as
contemplated in Regulation 35 of the 2005 Regulations was
taken, if so, in what manner.  The relevant orders/papers
concerning such relaxation, if any, shall also be brought
on record.

name of the selected candidates and their corresponding
qualifications.  The chart must carry a clarificatory note
against each such selected candidate whether they possess
the qualifications strictly as per the Regulations, 2005
or  they  possess  the  broader/  alternative/additional
qualifications  introduced  in  the  recruitment
advertisement/ notification.

material available on record, it is apparent that the petitioner
has sought transfer of H.M.O.P.No. 181/2021, titled as “Nekkanti
Surya Prabha Vs. Chitturi Balakrishna Chaitanya”, filed by the
respondent-wife under Section 9 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955,
and pending before the learned Senior Civil Judge, Narasapur, West
Godavari District, Andhra Pradesh.

this Court seeking transfer of the proceedings at a belated stage,
in the year 2026, when evidence is already being recorded before
the Family Court. The petitioner is contesting the proceedings for

1. Heard the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner.

there should not be multiplicity of examination of witnesses on one
and the same point. Trial Court should take care of this.

the petitioner.

same is completed, without fail, within a period of six months from
today.

time, if continued, it would be in the best interest of the child and we clarify that

report in a sealed cover to this Court for passing further orders.

“Learned counsel representing the petitioner,
Mr. Shishir Kr. Saxena submits that recently
the petitioner expressed his desire to engage

another counsel and the papers are returned to
the  petitioner.  As  such,  he  is  not  in  a

henceforthwith and oral prayer for a discharge
was made. In view of this submission of learned
counsel for the petitioner, issue notice to the
petitioner for engagement of another counsel
making the same returnable within six weeks.”
2. In pursuance of the said order notice was issued to the
petitioner for engagement of another counsel by registered A.D.
post.  The said notice was duly served upon the petitioner.
But despite that no one has entered appearance on his behalf as
indicated in office report dated 30.01.2025.  Thereafter, the
matter has been listed on various occasions but none has
appeared on behalf of the petitioner.  Today even on the second
call none put in appearance on behalf of the petitioner.
3. It is appears that petitioner is not interested in pursuing
the matter any further.
4. We, therefore, dismiss the Special Leave Petition for non-
prosecution.
